title: the push guard reads only a shell name's assignment after env, and env's -S string as one word
status: fixed after 0.5.0: the guard reads every word that holds a = after env's options as an assignment, a lone - there as -i, and env's -S string as the words env splits it into (DESIGN.md, 13)
world: memory; the git world runs it over real git (build step 6)

steps.note: each guard step is one of the guard grammar's commands, so the guard's answer is also judged by git's recorded one: env reads 1x=2 as an assignment, as it reads any word that holds a =, and runs git push origin main; under the mutant that reads after env only what the shell reads as an assignment, 1x=2 is read as the command env runs, the push passes and G11a is red here
GNU env reads the lone - after its options as -i, then A.B=1 as an assignment; under the mutant that reads no lone -, the - is read as the command and the forced push passes

args: nice env x-y=1 git push origin HEAD:board
steps.note: the same assignment behind nice: env reads x-y=1 as one, and the push to board is judged
env splits the string -S gives it into git, push, origin and main and runs them; under the mutant that splits no string, the string is one word, -S's value, and the push passes

b fetches in its second clone, b-other, makes a claim commit naming itself there, and runs env 1x=2 git -C ../b-other push --force-with-lease origin claude/1 from its session's clone, which never fetched claude/1: env runs git, which takes the lease in b-other, and the guard, judging the push there, refuses it; under the mutant that reads only a shell name's assignment after env, 1x=2 is read as the command, the lease is taken and G11a and G1 are red here
the same lease inside a string env's -S splits, env -S 'git -C ../b-other push --force-with-lease origin claude/1': under the mutant that splits no string it is not read at all

the same lease by git -C ../b-other after env GIT_DIR=<the clones>/b/.git, which prints env's environment and sets nothing in the shell, so git runs in b-other and the guard judges it there and refuses it; under the mutant that reads env's lone assignment as the shell's, the push is judged by its words and in b's own clone, which shows no claim file on origin/claude/1, so the fence cannot judge and the lease is taken: G11a and G1 are red here
